tickets.title: Third Avenue L stop closure pilot proposal
tickets.summary: A public speaker who simulated stop closures using MTA trip data argued that closing the Third Avenue L stop would save New Yorkers significant travel time because only about 5% of riders board or exit there. He noted the stop is not a transfer station and is not wheelchair accessible. Action: Refer the proposal to the transportation committee and ask the district office to explore a pilot stop closure with the MTA.

tickets.title: 11th Street e-bike storage and sidewalk obstruction
tickets.summary: Over 100 electric bikes used by food delivery workers are stored on 11th Street and nearby blocks around the clock, blocking the sidewalk and street and pushing businesses and landlords to suffer. Delivery workers have no legal parking or corral space, and the district manager said the NYPD plans an enforcement action on October 7 that would seize improperly parked bikes. Residents, the council office, and community groups asked for advance notice, translated and verbal outreach in the workers' languages, a two-week tagging period instead of seizure, and a follow-up conversation about the history of the block. Action: Ask the precinct and city agencies to provide advance notice in multiple languages, consider tagging before seizure, and find a legal parking site for the bikes.

tickets.title: Drug activity and lighting in Seward Park
tickets.summary: Residents and park users reported increased drug use, homelessness, and needle litter in Seward Park, and the Seward Park Conservancy and Lower East Side Ecology Center complained about conditions near a bathroom frequented by drug users. Members also noted dark areas and out lights in the park that let drug use go unseen. The district manager pointed to police presence, outreach contracts, and harm reduction services, and a member asked whether mobile crisis teams could be expanded to reduce drug use there. Action: Ask the precinct and Parks Department to address the drug activity, confirm light outages, and evaluate whether mobile crisis teams can respond instead of police.

tickets.title: Vincent Jenkins NYCHA food and communication access
tickets.summary: A speaker described struggling in NYCHA housing with lack of food, water, and necessities, and asked how people in poverty will get food. He also stated that deaf and hard-of-hearing residents need communication access, such as interpreters, during public meetings. Action: Follow up with NYCHA and social service providers about food and necessities for residents and about accessible communication at board meetings.

tickets.title: Liquor license denial for 11 Allen Street
tickets.summary: The board voted 20 yes, 10 no, and 9 abstaining to recommend straight denial of a full on-premises liquor license for the operator formerly of Time Cafe at 11 Allen Street, citing a problematic prior location, saturation, and crowds outside Time Cafe. Committee members noted the state could approve the license without community stipulations if the board does not appear at the SLA hearing. Community members spoke in opposition, including a resident of the Chinese-speaking community near the site. Action: Community board staff will organize residents to attend the SLA hearing and advocate for denial, and will pull 311 complaints and provide context.

tickets.title: Corrections to August SLA resolutions for two locations
tickets.summary: Two August SLA resolutions contained clerical errors: item 10 for Soft Tea House described a beer and wine license as a full on-premises license, and item 3 for Cozy Cafe had the same mismatch. The chair confirmed the resolutions should read recommendations to deny a beer and wine license unless stipulations are agreed to. Action: Correct the August SLA resolutions for items 3 and 10 to reflect beer and wine licenses before they are transmitted.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP postponement and community market terms
tickets.summary: The joint land use and economic development committee met with EDC about the Essex Market RFP, which was scheduled to be issued by the end of the month. EDC did not clearly show how the board's two resolutions on keeping a community market were incorporated. Action: Ask EDC to postpone issuing the RFP and hold a clarifying meeting with the land use chair and staff so the board's resolution requirements are included.

tickets.title: Free public restroom pilot in district
tickets.summary: The city is installing 17 free public restrooms citywide as a one-year pilot, with two in the district, including one near Delansancy Plaza and one at Cooper Square and East Sixth Street. Concerns were raised about access, who can use the restrooms, and emergency calls, and the restrooms are maintained by a private contractor. Action: Bring a resolution next month to set out the board's requests on access and operations during the pilot period.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge exits and Canal Street redesign update
tickets.summary: The transportation committee sent a letter to the mayor and DOT restating community concerns about the foot of the Manhattan Bridge exits after a recent fatal crash. The letter also asked for an update on the Canal Street redesign, since the board has not had one since January. Action: Follow up with DOT and the mayor's office for a response to the letter and an update on the Canal Street redesign.

tickets.title: Congestion pricing impact on FDR Drive
tickets.summary: A member asked whether congestion pricing caused the increased congestion on the FDR that the board had projected in an earlier resolution. The chair said this was not on the committee list but could be followed up. Action: Ask MTA or DOT to report on actual FDR congestion after congestion pricing and to return to the board to discuss it.

tickets.title: Transportation equity analysis and cross-town bus study
tickets.summary: The transportation committee worked with the Independent Budget Office on an equity analysis of how District 3 compares to other areas for transportation services. The top ideas include cross-town bus service and neighborhood parking locations. Action: Ask the IBO to complete research on cross-town buses and neighborhood parking as part of the equity analysis.

tickets.title: Proposed indoor roller skating venue on East River Pier
tickets.location_raw: East River Pier across from the Katherine Slip Mall
tickets.summary: A speaker proposed building a 300,000 square foot multi-use indoor roller skating facility on the East River Pier to fill a gap left by closed rinks. The proposal includes low admission pricing and claims 250 to 500 jobs. Action: Refer the proposal to the land use committee for review and ask the applicant to provide the site details.

tickets.title: East River Park stewardship facility construction delay
tickets.summary: The parks committee learned that part of the East River Park construction, the new facility that will house the Lower East Side Ecology Center and stewardship programs, is delayed by procurement challenges. The Parks Department offered to return with more detail and to address community requests for stewardship support in the interim. Action: Ask Parks to return with details on the procurement delay and interim stewardship support.

tickets.title: Mobile voting pilot for CEC elections
tickets.summary: A resolution would support a mobile voting option for Community Education Council elections to address very low turnout, which is about 2%, and digital access barriers for mobile-only households. Members raised concerns about immigrant families fearing data use, the need for clear eligibility messaging, and racial and class disparities in CEC membership. Action: Vote on the resolution and send it to the Department of Education's office of family and community empowerment urging a mobile pilot and expanded multilingual outreach.

tickets.title: Bylaws revision for attendance and removal process
tickets.summary: Proposed bylaw changes would address attendance by requiring a letter and meeting with the executive committee after the first attendance problem, separating attendance from the removal process, and requiring public members to follow conflict of interest policies. A member noted the wording gives the board chair and executive committee overlapping recommendation roles. Action: Vote on the proposed bylaw changes at the October full board meeting after the 28-day notice period.

tickets.title: Board trainings on SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures
tickets.summary: The board chair announced planned trainings on SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures for new and returning members, with dates to be announced later. The chair also asked members to submit training topics or questions by email. Action: Schedule the SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures trainings and share dates with members.

tickets.title: October district needs and budget priorities vote
tickets.summary: The board will vote in October on its district needs statement and ranked expense and capital budget priorities for city agencies, after district managers meet with over 20 agencies. The district manager noted the draft housing plan includes about 7,000 units, but 75% are market rate, while the board's top priority is affordable housing. Action: Hold the October committee and full board votes on district needs and ranked budget priorities, with affordable housing as a priority.

tickets.title: Draft housing plan comments and proactive committee positions
tickets.summary: The city's draft housing plan had a short comment window, so the board commented only from existing positions and district needs. A member asked whether there would be ongoing opportunities for land use input, and it was noted that shorter notice periods make proactive committee positions important. Action: Have the land use committee take proactive positions on housing plans and seek ongoing opportunities to comment.

tickets.title: Uptown MetroCard support for downtown residents
tickets.summary: A resident asked whether MetroCards or other transit support could be provided to help people travel to the new immigrant welcome center on 125th Street, since the trip takes about 60 minutes with transfers. The elected official's staff said they would raise the question with the community liaison. Action: Ask the elected official's office to address whether transportation cost assistance will be provided for the immigrant welcome center.
